why: Chapter on the term of an obligation: needed to say when a loan with no agreed term falls due; the record would cite whichever of articles 209 to 212 carries that rule (open point o2).
Chapter on the term of an obligation: a debt payable when the debtor is able, and the judge fixing a term (open point o2).
Chapter on the term of an obligation: loss of the benefit of the term, which would let the lender claim before the agreed term (boundary n1, open point o2).
Chapter on the term of an obligation: the judge fixing the term when none was agreed (open point o2).
Payment of what is not due: a boundary of the loan claim when no loan agreement can be proved would cite it (open point o4).
Unjust enrichment: to read around the boundary of a sum handed over without a proved loan agreement (open point o4).
List of commercial acts by their object, bank operations included: the section rule and boundary n7 would cite it to say when a loan is commercial (open point o3).
Accessory commercial acts: whether a trader's loan for his trade is commercial (open point o3).
Deposit: to tell a deposit of money from a loan for consumption (checklist k30, k40).
